name: Light Purplish Vinaceous
lede: Light Purplish Vinaceous is a pale, dusty mauve-pink from Ridgway's 1912 atlas, rarer in our painting archive than most of the colors in this group.

sections.title: A dusty mauve-pink
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 atlas carries this tone on plate XXXIX, hue 1‴, notated 0.1R 6.9/3.3 in the Munsell system [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary groups it under block 5, naming it moderate pink, 3.6 units from Ridgway's reading [1].

Its closest neighbor in our library is [[tuscany]], about 3.4 units away, almost the same color, followed by [[dawn]], about 4.1 units off and redder [2]. [[old-pink]] and [[old-pink]] sit a similar distance away, about 4.2 units off and more vivid [2]. "Vinaceous" again supplies the wine-colored base; "purplish" is Ridgway's modifier, not a separate dye or pigment name [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive matches this tone in 76 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.32 percent, as photographed, rarer than 52 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, present in 0.8 percent of the 1,674 paintings from that decade, 3.6 times its museums' expected rate [3].

Inside a painting it most often hides, in 44 percent of its 43 clearly-ranked appearances, a rank computed within each canvas so varnish cannot fake it [3]. It is also most over-represented in Indian paintings, 3.3 times the expected rate, found in 7 of the archive's 721 [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and the match is a computed color reading, not a pigment identification [3].
